motto: Serving Greywater Falls since 1887, and the lake somewhat longer.
weather: Overcast and mild for the season, 28°F, a soft haze sitting on the water since morning

undercurrent.phenomenon: an uncollected library card, due today, made out to nobody the town remembers
undercurrent.note: First business day back and the sixteenth square sits blank, which is the streak's first real interruption rather than a holiday alibi. Keeping level nearly flat (9 to 10) since Wren's own framing ('Friday isn't over yet') gives the town one more clean, deniable day before the blank square becomes a fact rather than a pause. Save the recognition beat (a hand placed) and the private-notes beat for after this squares one way or the other; if the sixteenth stamp does appear late Friday or over the weekend, that's the moment to start naming the pattern outright. Gerald's private aside about not writing something down is a small, deliberate crack worth returning to.

editor.name: Wren Aldercott
editor.voice: Dry, precise, allergic to drama, which is unfortunate given recent events. Writes like a person holding a clipboard while standing in rising water. Lets one true thing slip per edition, usually in the last line.

season_arc.premise: Calloway finishes reshelving the east alcove in the last cataloguer's 2009 order and finds, tucked behind where the ninth book sat, a library card checked out that same interrupted Wednesday and never returned. It is due back today. The borrower's name is nobody currently living in Greywater Falls has ever heard of, and the little pocket calendar stamped inside has fourteen years of due-date stamps on it already, one for every year since, each in a different hand.
